title: RuleCases -Case All under the engine's TEMP
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

rulecases-local-root-plus-dotnet-delete: needs first: Remove the shared fsa-tests base when it is left empty (non-recursive Directory.Delete, errors swallowed), or put the run folder directly in the TEMP so no base is created, then re-run the bug test. The diagnostic variant of the first option passed it.

dotnet-delete-under-real-windows-temp: needs first: Fix (a) must clear +R on read-only files before the Delete (for example a walk with [IO.File]::SetAttributes(f, Normal)), or fall back to such a walk when Delete throws UnauthorizedAccessException. Plain Delete(path,$true) is not equivalent to Remove-Item -Force.

Run-root predicate. The proposal moved RuleCases' scratch out of any TEMP a probe cannot list. This design uses TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's path rule, so one predicate governs TempTree, WindowCases and RuleCases, and the acceptance test keeps RuleCases' own removal under an unlistable parent in play. A reviewer may prefer the listability probe's generality.

Where the read-only fallback is proved. The proposal added a +R file to the acceptance test's stand-in. This design keeps the acceptance test byte-identical and proves the read-only, junction, already-gone and held-open shapes in a sibling AST-extraction test.

Whether the per-run root belongs in this slice at all. The proposal's own over-engineering note says the delete helper alone passes the acceptance test. The root is kept for findable killed-run leftovers (#373, Q-132) and can be dropped on its own.
Whether a failed scratch removal should fail the run (counted FAIL, exit 1) or only print a warning line.
A PowerShell mirror of ChooseTestsRoot in WindowCases (Get-CloudRigParent) versus hard-coding %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests, which is the same answer under both measured TEMPs.
Stale fsa-cf-* roots in the old location. The person clears them once, versus a legacy sweep kept in exempt TempTree.cs.
Get-CloudRigParent and any change to WindowCases' fsa-cf listings (decided finding M1).

The Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT run (Derived 7, and the three-run validate case from M5). It registers a real sync root and Q-086 gives that permission to validate, so it is owed to validate/person. SyncRootRig's new constructor lines are exercised by CloudRig.PrepareParent's default-suite Fact, not by the opt-in rig itself.
Redirecting the harness child's TEMP; harness.py's mkdtemp scratch still lands in the inherited TEMP and is removed there by the helper (design decision).
The non-material cases 'run is killed before its finally' and 'case folder 249 characters or longer'.
O-024 (GuardRule check for the Remove-Item rule) and O-025 (stale comments), both waived to the backlog.

Afterwards check that no sync root is registered and that %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests holds no fsa-cf-* folder. A failure not caused by the parent choice is recorded, not blamed on the routing (#201).

PERSON (administrator): fsa-settled-probe-* folders left directly in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP by my pre-fix SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells run, whose names I cannot list. They join the SC-214 / Q-219 leftovers (fsa-rules-*, fsa-*-case-*) for an elevated listing and removal. The two fsa-sl076-* folders my pre-fix SL-076 runs left there were removed by exact name.

deviation: M1 (decided): Get-CloudRigParent, its contract, case, TempRoots check and the WindowCases fitness rule were not built, and the engine-appended rule entry was deleted. WindowCases.ps1 changes only at the B-008 pad.

deviation: Get-ScratchParent takes three optional parameters (temp, Windows folder, LocalAppData) so its branches are fed directly, and it reads LocalApplicationData with GetFolderPath, as TempTree does, instead of $env:LOCALAPPDATA. It returns the temp path as given, with its trailing separator, so a drive-root TEMP stays absolute.

deviation: SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1 were changed more than the design said. The design asked SL-076 only to extract Remove-ScratchDir. I measured the HEAD copy of SL-076 under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: it already failed there (ShortName finds no 8.3 name, its own cleanup is denied). SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells exited 1 under that TEMP and left fsa-settled-probe-* folders. Both now use Get-ScratchParent and Remove-ScratchDir, so the M2/M3 commands can pass under both TEMPs.

deviation: m1: the review was right that Directory.Delete unlinks a junction before it stops on a read-only file. The walk's reparse rule is therefore tested by extracting the nested Open-Tree and feeding it a junction, not only through Remove-ScratchDir.

deviation: m2 'before' evidence uses the design-literal pre-fix variants (Write-Output scratch line, no Out-Host at the two sites, no Out-Null on `& $change`) built from the fixed file. HEAD never had a scratch line, so there was no HEAD code to fail the rows. Beyond the review's two sites I also fixed the early-return Check and `& $change` in New-RowsFile.

deviation: Check commands that need TEMP set (C-002, C-003, C-008, C-009) are wrapper scripts, SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 and SL-098-B008Root.Tests.ps1, because a test_command cannot carry shell syntax and M4 forbids setting TEMP through a quoted -Command.

deviation: Standing rule on outside defects: no KnownWorkarounds entry or setting was built. The defect avoided (PowerShell's Remove-Item listing the parent) is avoided only in tests/rules and test scripts, which are not shipped, and the design decided this explicitly. A checkbox in the app's Settings window would govern nothing the app does. Recorded so a reviewer can overrule.

deviation: O-024 and O-025 are waived (SC-223, SC-224): the GuardRule check for the Remove-Item rule is not built, and the stale %TEMP% comments in CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:19, :251 and CloudRig.cs:10, :22 are left. Only the comment that said the rig was exempt was rewritten, and SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json's two notes about the exemption were updated to match the fitness change.

drift: M5's because-text puts choose, create and sweep 'into one helper in SyncRootRig'. The build put it in CloudRig.PrepareParent, as M5's fix text named it. That is the only place a default-suite Fact can reach it, because SyncRootRig is private to the Trait-gated class. The build summary states it but does not mark it as a choice between the two wordings.

drift: Standing rule on outside defects: the PowerShell Remove-Item workaround (IsReparsePointLikeSymlink lists the parent, PowerShell#16804) is unconditional and has no KnownWorkarounds entry. That matches the design's explicit key decision and is recorded as a deviation. It lives only in test scripts, a comment in RuleCases.ps1 names the defect and the upstream issue, and a setting would govern nothing the app does.

drift: Get-ScratchParent returns the temp path with its trailing separator and reads LocalApplicationData through GetFolderPath, not $env:LOCALAPPDATA. Both are declared. Its at-or-under test (GetFullPath plus StartsWith) is not TempTree's Scanner.IsAtOrUnder over LongPath.NormalizeRoot, so the two can disagree for a TEMP spelled with a \\?\ prefix. No measured TEMP is spelled that way.

drift: No undeclared departure was found. The SL-076 and SettledCountProbe rework, the m2 extras (the early-return Check and `& $change | Out-Null`) and the SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json note edits are all declared.

Two differences earlier stages flagged were not reproduced: SC-215 (Remove-Item denied under the engine token) and SC-216 (a possible TMPDIR in the stage shell).

critique missed: The critique (M2, M3) put SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 and SettledCountProbe.ps1 into the cases to be run under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. It never asked whether those scripts root scratch in GetTempPath() or use Remove-Item themselves, which lesson #372 had handed over. Both already failed under that TEMP at HEAD (SL-076: ShortName and its own denied cleanup; SettledCountProbe -Shape BothShells: exit 1). The build had to rewrite both beyond the design, and its first runs of the unfixed scripts left fsa-settled-probe-* and two fsa-sl076-* folders in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. A check would be: for every script a case adds to the TEMP matrix, grep it for GetTempPath, $env:TEMP and Remove-Item before listing it as a consumer.

critique missed: The design marked 'RuleCases killed before its finally runs' as non-material (no test), and the critique did not challenge it. Q-132 already said killed runs are the main source of leaked scratch. In practice -Case All (~360 s) is killed at about 120 s by whatever drives it. Validate found four fsa-rulecases-* roots of 140-141 folders each, started exactly 2 minutes apart, and had to kill a C-004 run by hand to prove the leftovers are findable. A check would be: the critique should ask what the leftover looks like and who removes it, and require a kill-mid-run case when the loop's own timeouts are known to be shorter than the run.

code-review missed: Remove-ScratchDir leaves behind a junction that is itself marked ReadOnly. It records one 'cleanup:' FAIL and throws nothing; the outside files stay untouched. Code review round 2 tried six shapes (read-only subfolder, read-only top folder, Hidden+System+ReadOnly file, nested read-only folders, trailing separator, file at path) and declared 'found nothing new', but fed no read-only reparse point. The critique's m1 fix asked for unlinking each reparse point and likewise did not ask about +R on the link. Validate's independent O-014 probe (entry j2ro, attrib +r /L) found it.

SC-215 (Remove-Item denied under the engine token) and SC-216 (a possible TMPDIR in the stage shell) were not reproduced. Whether [IO.Directory]::Delete of the harness's fsa-rules-* scratch in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP works under the engine token is unmeasured.

SL-098 appended another marker, so that red persists.

still unknown: What drives RuleCases -Case All and kills it at about 120 s? Four fsa-rulecases-* roots started at 2-minute intervals suggest a 120 s timeout, but who ran them and with what limit was not observed.

still unknown: Did validate's Engine-TEMP -Case All leave any harness fsa-rules-* folder directly in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP? This user cannot list it. The only evidence is that the helper printed no 'cleanup:' line. Older leftovers there (SC-214, Q-219, fsa-settled-probe-*) still need an elevated listing.

went wrong: The design built a whole component set (Get-CloudRigParent, its contract, case, TempRoots check, and the WindowCases fitness rule) on the investigation's wrong account of WindowCases.ps1:5680/:5747. The design stage did not read those lines, and its own hedge ('if they turn out not to look for SyncRootRig's roots, they are left alone') contradicted its contracts. The engine had already appended the matching fitness rule, so the build had to delete an engine-written entry by hand.

went wrong: The critique halted once with 10 findings, 5 of them major (M1 wrong WindowCases account; M2 SL-076 broken unnamed; M3 5.1 compatibility; M4 TEMP assignment in a quoted -Command; M5 opt-in rig unexecuted). All were real. The design's brief was only a title and five merged complaints, and the design leaned on the investigation rather than the files.

went wrong: The build-check could not find the engine's venv python because it searched only inside taad_v3, so Derived 3 (-Case All with a listable TEMP) stayed 'unknown' until the design pointed at %APPDATA%\taad3\venv. It also triggered the 300 MB SDK download again.

went wrong: The build ran the unfixed SettledCountProbe and SL-076 under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and left fsa-settled-probe-* and fsa-sl076-* folders there. The fsa-sl076-* ones were removed by exact name; the fsa-settled-probe-* ones need an administrator, adding to the Q-219 pile.

went wrong: The build declared O-020 discharged while sending the real Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT run to a person, which contradicted Q-086 and M5. Code review caught it and the engine waived it (O-026). Validate ran the three runs anyway, so the waiver text 'nothing else is sending this stage back' was wrong.

went wrong: Code review ran twice. The first round halted on 4 'undeclared departures' that were all declared or decided, and one entry literally reads 'No undeclared departure was found', so the halt cost a lap. Its two real minors were waived to the backlog: SC-225 (the wrapper's default -EngineRoot only resolves from a slice worktree, so the documented commands in SL-098-RuleCasesUnderTemps.Tests.ps1 fail from the main checkout) and SC-226.

went wrong: Shipped with known loose ends: stale %TEMP% comments (CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:19 and :251, CloudRig.cs:10 and :22, SC-224), no repo test showing the new RuleCases Remove-Item fitness rule can fire (SC-223; code review checked it by hand only), and a read-only junction that Remove-ScratchDir leaves behind with a counted FAIL.

went wrong: The bug report had only a title, so two readings had to be assumed. One was that 'RuleCases.ps1 is not touched by this slice' was SL-091's filing note, not a limit on SL-098; it is unconfirmed by a person.
